text:
Don't Move - Official Clip (2026)
They called for help...but no one could locate them to save them. 

An annual camping trip takes a horrifying turn when a church group mistakenly hikes into an unknown area of a remote forest and finds themselves hunted by a giant, terrifying creature.

Check out this clip from Don't Move, an upcoming horror movie starring Lyndsy Fonseca (Kick-Ass franchise, Hot Tub Time Machine) and rapper/singer/songwriter Russ (M. Night Shyamalan’s Trap), with Tom Cavanagh (‘The Flash,’ ‘DC’s Legends of Tomorrow’), Hunter King (Holiday Touchdown), Joseph Lee Anderson (Tyler Perry’s Divorce in Black, ‘Young Rock’), and Rob Riggle (The Hangover, Step Brothers) alongside a special appearances by T-Pain (Furious 7), Brian "Q" Quinn ('Impractical Jokers') and Matt Biedel ('The Fall of the House of Usher').

Based on the bestselling horror novel, Don't Move was co-written and produced by James “Murr” Murray, one of the stars of the long-running hit TV show Impractical Jokers. 

Directed by Maclain Nelson and written by Murray, Nelson and Darren Wearmouth, the film was produced by Murray, David M. Wulf (The Card Counter, Call Jane, Return To Silent Hill) and Ethan Berman. 

Don't Move opens in theaters nationwide today, Friday, September 11, 2026.

text:
PlayStation Ditched Hideo Kojima's Physint Over Budget Concerns and Missed Deadlines - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
More details are coming to light surrounding Sony's decision to part ways with Hideo Kojima's Physint project. According to reports, the game was already missing deadlines, was in danger of being overbudget, and was still years away from release. Sony has had a string of high-profile flops and cancelations—especially in the live-service space—so it seems like the company was looking to trim budget wherever it could. In other news, another Sony-related property has popped up under a different name. What looks like a trailer for the extraction shooter Fairgame$ has appeared, but under the name Project Espresso. The curious can sign up for a private playtest coming soon. And finally, we have a breakdown of all the big new gaming releases of the week.

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 Review
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 reviewed by Will Borger on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

"Fireteam Elite 2 doesn’t reinvent the wheel. It’s best alongside three friends for a full squad, but it’s fun enough solo as well. The story isn’t anything to write home about, but the characters are likeable, the missions are fun, and the new Specialist class provides a cool way to further customize your kit. There are some bugs in this bug hunt, but they don’t distract from the action too much. Turns out blasting Xernos and synths is a good time with friends, and there is a lot of blasting to be done thanks to the Horde mode and a smart unlockable system that encourages you to replay levels, explore each class, and try new things. It may not quite be a glorious day in the corps, but it’s damn close."

Dive! Punch! Catch! Sea Sniffers is a unique take on collecting fish where you play as a seal that throws a mean punch. Check out the Sea Sniffers announcement trailer for this upcoming game to see gameplay, characters, and more. Sea Sniffers will be available on Steam in 2027.

In Sea Sniffers, explore sunken ships, uncover hidden caves, and meet the ocean’s eccentric inhabitants, whose mischievous stories range from silly escapades to chaotic adventures. In Sea Sniffers, quirky quests weave together a blend of RPG-progression and offbeat storytelling.
